correctness.rationale: Every pattern with a descent must include the original first entry and is uniquely a grid element tau_(a,b) with 1<=a<=k-1 and 0<=b<=n-k; all others are identities iota_s. Length ranks and longest increasing subsequences force all covers to be identity-chain edges, identity-to-tau bridge edges, or two-coordinate grid edges. The specified labels s,n,a+1,(k-1)+b+1 are strictly increasing for exactly one lex-minimal maximal chain in each of the three possible interval types; a premature bridge labeled n would have to be followed by a smaller label. Reverse-complement preserves pattern order. I wrote a separate exact subsequence poset checker, enumerating every family through n=8 (28 n,k families, 5132 maximal-chain tests) and independently matching the label condition; the universal proof rests on the complete element/order description, not bounded enumeration. Degenerate k=2,k=n,n=2 included.
